name: Trumaí
confidence_why: one confirmed first-hand source; 6 other works read were silent
catalog_quote: Stress always falls on the final syllable of the word. Phonetic correlates of stress are greater intensity and higher pitch than preceding syllables. (Guirardello 1999)

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Coding fixed-strict final stress rests on the standard reference grammar (Guirardello 1999, Rice PhD, 452 pp), which we hold as the original Rice bitstream plus scanned; the deciding sentence 'Stress always falls on the final syllable of the word' is verified verbatim at printed p.7 (PDF p.33), and the grammar's other stress remarks (postpositions independently stressed, p.75; stressed vs cliticized auxiliary allomorphs, p.141) do not disturb a word-domain final-stress coding. No phonetic/prosodic study of Trumai exists in Crossref or SAPhon, and the only newer description is a 2023 handbook sketch by the same author (paywalled). The record's top-level quote/cite/grade fields are empty while the verified primary quotation sits in sources[0]; promote it to the deciding quote and set the strength of the evidence to primary-verified. If the blank grade is by design for database-derived rows, action is 'n
